_: Controls under 44x44 per screen, MEASURED (not estimated). Every number is a debt with a name. It may only ever go DOWN: touch-targets.mjs fails if one climbs, and also if one falls without this file being tightened, because that slack is where a regression would hide. Drive a screen to 0 and it stays at 0 for ever.
_started_at: 233 across 21 screens. Shared chrome took it to 128: the theme toggle (28px, every screen), the section switcher (32px, every screen, shipped by me that same morning) and the bottom tab bar (a 42px hit area inside a 64px bar, five times per screen). Then the costing checkboxes and the briefing rows took it to 114, and the one shared SearchField took it to 107.
_2026_08_30_searchfield: 114 -> 107, and three more screens to zero (product-card, stock-ops, suppliers). Thirteen hand-written search bars became one component. Each was a fixed-height wrapper around a bare flex-1 input, and a flex child with no height sizes to its own line box -- so a bar that drew at 44-52px accepted taps on about 20px of itself. Customers only moved 28 -> 27 because 27 of its findings are the A-Z rail, not the search bar.
_whats_left: Segmented-control tabs at 23-37px (products, financials, competitors, inventory, reorder, reports) and a handful of icon and pill buttons four pixels short. The search-field shape is gone: one component owns it now, so it cannot come back one screen at a time.
_customers: 27 of these are the A-Z index rail: 27 letters at 22x19. That is Apple's own Contacts geometry -- it is a SCRUB control, not 27 discrete targets, and enlarging it would break the pattern it copies. It needs a documented exemption in the audit rather than a change to the rail, and until that exists it sits here as a number rather than being silently excluded.
